agentCan: Build the /wc-auth/v1/authorize URL and capture the key pair POSTed to the callback URL
Call the REST API with the keys (Basic Auth over HTTPS, or OAuth 1.0a one-legged signing over HTTP)
Detect 401 'Consumer Key is invalid' failures and prompt for reconnection

approval.cost: None documented for generating keys or using the auth endpoint
approval.trigger: No review, approval, registration, or listing is required at any point in the documented REST API connection flows. There is no WooCommerce central authority that approves integrations: authorization is granted locally, per store, by that store's admin clicking accept (auth endpoint) or generating a key (manual flow). Pre-approval caps: none documented (there is no approval state to be 'pre'). The WooCommerce Marketplace referenced in the docs is for buying/selling extensions (plugins); it is not a gate for REST API connections.
approval.wait: Not applicable (no review exists in the docs read)

blockers.detail: If the store admin revokes the key (or deletes the linked WordPress user), your integration simply starts failing with 401 ('Consumer Key is invalid'); WooCommerce documents no webhook/notification to the connecting app for key revocation.
blockers.howToClear: Monitor for 401s and build a reconnect prompt; you cannot be notified proactively.
blockers.title: No revocation callback to you

blockers.detail: Keys are 'linked to a WordPress user on your site'; the key's effective access combines the key permission level with that user's account. Deleting or demoting that user breaks the integration.
blockers.howToClear: Ask the store to link keys to a dedicated, stable admin user.
blockers.title: Keys inherit the linked user's risk

blockers.detail: 'The Consumer Secret is shown only once. Copy and store it in a safe place before leaving the page.' In the auth-endpoint flow, if you fail to persist the POSTed keys, the store admin must redo the flow.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the callback POST body immediately and durably (read the raw POST body, not form fields).
blockers.title: Secret capture is one-shot

alternatives: Manual key copy/paste (the store admin generates a key in wp-admin and pastes the consumer key/secret and site URL into your service; the Consumer Secret 'is shown only once')
flavor.recommended: The Authentication Endpoint flow (/wc-auth/v1/authorize), which delivers a per-store API key pair to your callback URL
flavor.why: There is no centralized 'app' object and no WooCommerce-run OAuth program. WooCommerce is self-hosted (a WordPress plugin), so the credential object is a per-store REST API key pair generated inside each store's WordPress admin: a Consumer Key (ck_...) and Consumer Secret (cs_...), each set linked to a specific WordPress user on that store, with a single coarse permission level (Read, Write, or Read/Write). 'Most integrations require you to generate API keys in WooCommerce and enter them in the external service to establish the connection.' The Authentication Endpoint flow 'can be used by any app to allow users to generate API keys. This makes integration with WooCommerce API simpler because the user only needs to access a URL and click accept. After being redirected back to the app, the API keys will be sent in a POST request.' What it delivers is still a static key pair, not a token. Over HTTPS, requests authenticate with the keys as HTTP Basic Auth; over plain HTTP, requests must be signed with OAuth 1.0a 'one-legged' authentication (a request-signing scheme for the key pair, not a 3-legged authorization program).

humanMust: (Store admin) Visit the authorize URL, log in, and click accept (auth-endpoint flow), or generate the key manually under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API
(Store admin, manual flow) Copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret (shown once) into the connecting application
name: WooCommerce
nuances: HTTPS asymmetry and signing traps: over plain HTTP you must implement OAuth 1.0a one-legged signing with strict signature-base-string rules (use the exact store URL from the API index, e.g. with/without www; the request body is NOT signed; percent-encoding double-encodes % as %25). 'The REST API will deny any requests that include a timestamp outside of a 15 minute window to prevent replay attacks', the only time figure in the docs read.

Server quirk: some servers don't parse the Authorization header ('Consumer key is missing'); the documented fallback is passing consumer_key/consumer_secret as query-string parameters, which leaks secrets into URLs and logs.
The docs warn verbatim that the auth endpoint 'is used only to make easy integration with WooCommerce REST API. THIS NOT INTENDED TO BE USED AS A LOGIN ENDPOINT FOR CUSTOMERS!'

'The legacy REST API has been removed from WooCommerce core'; integrations needing it must install the separate WooCommerce Legacy REST API plugin and enable it under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Legacy API, and legacy-API webhooks stop working without it. The manual flow also requires pretty permalinks set to anything other than 'Plain', and the REST API enabled under WooCommerce > Settings.
prerequisites: A live WooCommerce store URL (self-hosted WordPress + WooCommerce)
A callback URL served over HTTPS (for the auth-endpoint flow)
Secure storage for the per-store key pair

steps.detail: Build https://{store}/wc-auth/v1/authorize with mandatory parameters app_name, scope (read / write / read_write), user_id (your own app's user ID, 'NOT THE USER ID IN WOOCOMMERCE'), return_url, and callback_url (must be HTTPS). The store admin visits the URL, logs in, and clicks accept on the authorization screen.
steps.title: Build the authorize URL; store admin accepts

steps.detail: The store POSTs JSON to your callback_url: { key_id, user_id, consumer_key, consumer_secret, key_permissions }. Store them immediately (in PHP, read the raw POST body, not $_POST). The user's browser is redirected to return_url with success (1 = approved, 0 = denied) and user_id query parameters.
steps.title: Receive the key pair at your callback URL

steps.detail: Call https://{store}/wp-json/wc/v3/... with Basic Auth using the key/secret over HTTPS. Over plain HTTP, sign requests with OAuth 1.0a one-legged authentication instead.
steps.title: Call the REST API

steps.detail: WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API > Add Key: enter a Description, select the WordPress User the key is generated for, select Permissions (Read / Write / Read/Write), Generate API Key, and copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret (shown once) into the connecting application. Pretty permalinks must be enabled (anything other than 'Plain').
steps.title: Manual alternative: admin generates a key in wp-admin

tagline: WooCommerce runs no OAuth program: the connection credential is a per-store API key pair (linked to a WordPress user, one of three coarse permission levels), delivered either by an admin in wp-admin or through the Authentication Endpoint flow, which POSTs the keys to your callback after the admin clicks accept.

time.active: ~5 min per store + ~1 hr of API code
time.total: Same day; no approval wait exists
